claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase heterogeneity.
The proposed PINN will explicitly embed elasticity and plasticity laws and accept local composition fluctuations, phase fraction, and interface density as inputs.
The training dataset will contain approximately 100–200 points from high-fidelity simulations and small-scale tensile and fracture experiments.
The model will be trained at room temperature and validated at loading rates extending to moderate values.
Local chemical fluctuations influence dislocation motion and associated strengthening.
Phase fractions and interface densities mediate dislocation motion in the target heterostructure.
Local composition fluctuations, phase fractions, and interface densities mediate crack propagation.
Embedding conservation laws and constitutive relations will keep network predictions physically realistic when training data are limited.
Physics constraints will reduce the amount of training data required and thereby address computational inefficiency.
Representing key microstructural influences will enable the network to predict complex fracture behavior.
The PINN will predict Young's modulus of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with an error within ±5–10%.
The PINN will predict yield strength of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with an error within ±5–10%.
The PINN will predict fracture toughness of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 with an error within ±15%.
The PINN will provide at least a fivefold computational-efficiency gain over full-scale simulation methods.
First-principles and molecular-dynamics methods have higher computational demands than the proposed PINN.
Traditional simulations and some unconstrained machine-learning approaches can have prediction errors exceeding ±10–20% for the targeted properties.
The approach will remain reliable at room temperature, at moderate loading rates, and while the reported hierarchical heterostructure is maintained.
The approach may cease to be reliable for substantially altered microstructures or extreme loading conditions absent from training.
Predictive accuracy will depend on whether the augmented dataset adequately represents the diversity of microstructural states and failure mechanisms.
Charpy or micro-tensile fracture tests can be used to determine the fracture-toughness target in the blinded benchmark.
